title: Approving an app pause can hand free days to a member whose plan ends before the pause starts, or has already ended
what: A member can ask in the app to pause any days starting up to 90 days ahead, as long as their plan has not ended on the day they ask. The pause does not have to fall inside the plan. When the desk taps Approve, the full number of paused days is added to the end of the plan, with no check that the plan still runs or that the pause starts before it ends. So a member whose plan ends on 25 Nov can ask to pause 1 Dec to 28 Feb; Approve moves the end to late February and he trains for three months free. A request left waiting until after the plan ended is approved the same way. The card shows only the pause dates, not when the plan ends, so the desk has nothing to warn them. The Bring a friend reward, by contrast, refuses a plan that has ended.
expected: Only the paused days that fall inside the plan are added, and a plan that has already ended cannot be paused. The card shows the plan's last day next to the pause and says plainly when the pause starts after it.
how_often: whenever a member asks to pause near or after the end of the plan
fix_line: Add only the paused days inside the plan, refuse a plan that has ended, and show the plan's end on the request card

items.reason: Web panel logic: no install package, sideload, Play package, watch or phone version split here. Data kept across updates is handled: the staff job kept on one browser before the server had it is sent once later; the dots and What's new seen marks tolerate bad or old storage; old receipt numbers never change when the long-number rule came. The panel's Refresh only re-reads data and never reloads the page, so a tab left open across a deploy keeps the old logic and is never told to reload (same fault as FN-B-time-panel-assistant-01).

Trial end and paid-plan end use India days and only change words. Plan end: a pause approved after or beyond the plan's end adds free days (new 01). Month ends: a monthly plan started on the 29th to 31st is cut short (same as FN-B-time-panel-forms-01). Year end: receipt series restart on 1 April by the payment day. Leap day: birthdays and join anniversaries on 29 Feb fall on 28 Feb. Member returns: a join-online request opens the usual Add member form with its archived-number banner. Staff leaving is handled in sign-in code outside this area. Not opened for months: What's new shows the last 3 updates only, dots end after 30 days.

Rules added later in this area apply to existing gyms too: the 'dots only for features after your gym joined' rule reads the gym's set-up time for every gym; the long-receipt-number rule keeps old numbers; numbers are stored in one form so the 10-digit cut does not split old members from new.
Existing users have a path: jobs kept on a browser before the server could save them are sent once it can; an owner on a new browser gets the newest update remembered and later ones shown.
Rule applied: no new-users-only flow without a path found in this area.

A brand-new gym: dots skip any feature dated on or before the gym's set-up day and are owner-only, never in the demo. The What's new card shows nothing on a browser's first visit (the newest update is only remembered), and nothing in the demo gym. The bell's MettleUp messages for a new gym are logic-1's FN-B-time-panel-logic-1-04, outside this area.
Rule applied: no new mark in this area lands on something that was already there when the gym joined.
